gold_sql:
SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(DISTINCT b.class_symbol_id) AS subclasses
FROM code.symbols s
JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = s.file_id
JOIN code.class_bases b ON b.base_symbol_id = s.symbol_id
JOIN code.symbols sub ON sub.symbol_id = b.class_symbol_id
JOIN code.files sf ON sf.file_id = sub.file_id
WHERE s.kind = 'class' AND s.is_public AND NOT f.is_test AND NOT sf.is_test
  AND f.file_id LIKE 'auto_ontology/connectors/%'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM code.calls c WHERE c.callee_symbol_id = s.symbol_id AND c.call_kind = 'direct')
GROUP BY s.symbol_id
ORDER BY s.symbol_id;

agent_answer: This query finds public classes in auto_ontology/connectors that are used only as base classes, subclassed by other non-test classes but never constructed by a resolved call, and gives the number of non-test subclasses of each. It starts from the class_bases table joined with symbols on base_symbol_id = symbol_id, then joins the files table on symbols.file_id = files.file_id to filter out test files. The WHERE clause filters for public symbols (is_public = True), non-test base names (base_name NOT LIKE 'test_%'), and class kind (kind = 'class'). The GROUP BY groups results by base class name, and the HAVING clause ensures only base classes with at least one non-test subclass are included. The COUNT(symbols.symbol_id) gives the number of non-test subclasses for each base class.
